title: Systems & Workflow Automation Engineer – Remote
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE



Éclat Financial Consultancy is seeking a highly technical and process-oriented Systems & Workflow Automation Engineer to systemize and automate our operations—from client onboarding through service fulfillment.



Your primary responsibility will be to review our existing procedures, identify manual or repetitive steps, and build dependable automated workflows connecting our accounting, tax, client management, communication, and AI systems.



This is a hands-on role for someone who can understand how a professional services firm operates and turn those processes into organized, documented, and scalable systems.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES



1.) Review and map our current workflows from lead intake and proposal acceptance through onboarding, service delivery, billing, and client follow-up.



2.) Identify bottlenecks, repetitive tasks, process gaps, and opportunities for automation.



3.) Build automated workflows connecting platforms through APIs, webhooks, MCP connections, and third-party automation tools.



4.) Integrate Ignition with our internal systems and AI agents.



5.) Create an automated process that detects an accepted Ignition proposal and retrieves structured information, including:



A.) Client details



B.) Accepted services



C.) Pricing



D.) Billing schedules



E.) Engagement information



6.) Automatically notify the appropriate team members after an engagement is accepted.



7.) Trigger the correct client onboarding workflow based on the services included in the signed proposal.



8.) Create client records, tasks, folders, internal notifications, and follow-up steps without unnecessary manual data entry.



9.) Connect systems such as Ignition, TaxDome, accounting applications, email, Google Workspace, and other platforms used by the firm.



10.) Develop reliable AI-assisted workflows for reading, organizing, summarizing, and routing client information.



11.) Build safeguards to prevent duplicate records, incomplete onboarding, incorrect assignments, and missed client requests.



12.) Test all workflows before implementation and troubleshoot failed automations.



13.) Create monitoring and error-alert systems so the team is notified whenever an automation fails.



14.) Maintain data security and protect confidential client and tax information.



15.) Prepare clear standard operating procedures, workflow diagrams, and technical documentation.



16.) Train team members on newly implemented systems.



17.) Continuously review and improve existing workflows as the firm grows.



INITIAL PRIORITY PROJECT



The first major project will involve improving our engagement acceptance and onboarding process.



When a client signs an engagement through Ignition, the system should:



1.) Detect that the proposal has been accepted.



2.) Retrieve the proposal details through the Ignition MCP connection or another appropriate integration.



3.) Extract the client’s information, selected services, pricing, and billing schedule.



4.) Provide the information to our internal AI agent.



5.) Notify the appropriate department or team members.



6.) Create and assign the necessary onboarding tasks.



7.) Initiate the correct workflow based on the services accepted.



8.) Save the relevant engagement information in the appropriate client record.



9.) Confirm that the onboarding process was successfully initiated.



10.) Alert the appropriate person if any part of the automation fails.



REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS



A.) Proven experience building business process automations and system integrations.



B.) Strong experience working with APIs, webhooks, and structured data.



C.) Experience with automation platforms such as Make, Zapier, n8n, Power Automate, or similar tools.



D.) Experience designing AI-agent workflows or integrating AI tools with business applications.



E.) Ability to understand a manual business process and convert it into a dependable automated workflow.



F.) Strong troubleshooting, testing, and problem-solving skills.



G.) Ability to create organized technical documentation and standard operating procedures.



H.) Excellent attention to detail.



I.) Strong written and verbal English communication skills.



J.) Ability to work independently, manage priorities, and provide regular progress updates.



K.) Understanding of data privacy, access controls, and the proper handling of confidential client information.



PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS



A.) Experience with Ignition, including its API or MCP connection.



B.) Experience with TaxDome or another accounting practice-management platform.



C.) Experience integrating Google Workspace, email, accounting software, CRM systems, and project-management tools.



D.) Familiarity with accounting, bookkeeping, tax preparation, or another professional services environment.



E.) Experience working with AI assistants, large language models, and document-processing automations.



F.) Experience developing dashboards, monitoring systems, and error logs.



G.) Basic programming or scripting experience using Python, JavaScript, or a similar language.



THE IDEAL CANDIDATE



The ideal candidate is not simply familiar with automation tools. We need someone who can examine an entire workflow, understand how each department is affected, and build a practical system that the team can depend on.



You should be comfortable asking detailed questions, challenging inefficient processes, and recommending better solutions. You must also be able to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical team members.



SUCCESS IN THIS ROLE MEANS



A.) Less manual data entry and fewer repetitive administrative tasks.



B.) Faster and more consistent client onboarding.



C.) Clear ownership and automatic assignment of responsibilities.



D.) Fewer missed steps, duplicate records, and communication gaps.



E.) Proper documentation for every automated process.



F.) Reliable workflows with appropriate testing, monitoring, and error handling.



G.) Systems that can scale as the firm adds more clients and team members.



HOW TO APPLY



Please submit the following:



1.) Your résumé.



2.) A brief introduction explaining your experience with workflow automation and system integration.



3.) Examples of automations or integrations you have personally designed and implemented.



4.) A list of the automation platforms, APIs, AI tools, and business systems you have used.



5.) A brief explanation of how you would approach the following project:



“When a client accepts an Ignition proposal, automatically retrieve the client, service, pricing, and billing information; notify the correct team members; and initiate the appropriate onboarding workflow.”



6.) Your expected compensation.



7.) Your availability and preferred working schedule.



8.) A short video introduction discussing one automation project you completed, the problem it solved, and the result achieved.



Please begin your application with the words “Éclat Automation” so we know you carefully reviewed the complete posting.



Applications without relevant automation or system-integration experience will not be considered.

title: Crypto BD Lead (Player-Coach)
description:
How to apply

Applications missing any item are auto-rejected. Send:



1. Loom video (2-3 min): who you are, your crypto experience, the most qualified appointments you've personally booked in one month, and how you'd produce 5 qualified GMI partnership calls per week.

2. In writing (3-4 sentences): what a launchpad is and why one would want LP Bonds for its projects.

3. Scenario: "Your reps sent 250 targeted messages in one week, received 18 positive replies, and booked zero qualified calls. What do you inspect, and what do you change in the next 48 hours?"

4. One target for GMI (a DEX, launchpad, or ecosystem): why it's qualified, the exact role you'd contact, the channel, and the personalized first message you'd send.

5. Your
 handle, available hours in GMT+8, and earliest start date.



Subject line must start with: BOND OPS





At target pace this role pays roughly $1,500 to $2,500/month depending on how many appointments you book personally vs through your reps, with no cap on the upside. Base is the floor, not the offer.



About GMI

GonnaMakeIt (GMI) built LP Bonds, a live DeFi liquidity product deployed across 9+ EVM chains (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and more).

LP Bonds lock liquidity for 20 years while giving users a tradeable Bond NFT earning
% APR. The liquidity is locked, the user is not: they can sell their Bond NFT anytime. Rewards accrue inside the bond instead of being farmed and dumped.

Our partnership targets: DEXs, token launchpads, L1/L2 blockchain ecosystems, and select token projects with strong strategic fit.

We need someone to build and run a BD engine that consistently puts qualified partnership calls on the founder's calendar.





The role

One job: produce qualified partnership calls that actually happen, every week.



The founder takes the calls and closes. You own everything before that: rep recruiting and management, target selection, qualification, outreach strategy, follow-up, pipeline, booking, call prep, and funnel diagnosis.



This is a player-coach role. You manage commission-based BD reps AND personally do outreach and book calls whenever the team is below target. Meetings, training, recruiting, and spreadsheet work do not count as output. Qualified calls held count as output.





The metric



Qualified partnership appointments held per week. After ramp: floor 2, target 5, strong 6+.



A call counts only when ALL are true: the target passes our qualification standard, the attendee is a decision-maker (or credible sponsor with direct access to one), they explicitly expressed interest in LP Bonds for their org, they know what the call is about, the call happens, a real partnership discussion occurs, and the founder confirms it was qualified.



Does NOT count: no-shows, reschedules until held, calls where they pitch their product to us, generic networking, community mods who can't advance a deal, duplicates, or projects that can't realistically use LP Bonds.





What you own

1. Rep performance. Audit the existing rep team immediately. Recruit replacements as needed. Give each rep target accounts, messaging, channels, and weekly numbers. Coach producers, cut non-producers. A rep showing no meaningful pipeline progress after 10 working days gets diagnosed and acted on, not carried for 30.

2. Targeting. At least 80% of the active pipeline is DEXs, launchpads, and L1/L2 ecosystems. Targets are EVM-compatible unless the founder approves an exception. Do not fill the pipeline with projects just because they're easy to reach.

3. Qualification. You run (or audit) our LP Bonds Partner Assessment on every interested project. Score of 5/10+ passes to the founder. Below 5 can be escalated for founder review if you believe it's a real opportunity. Before any prospect reaches the founder you confirm: real scale/traction, a genuine LP Bonds fit, a decision-maker in the loop, and explicit interest in LP Bonds for THEM. "We want to explore this for our ecosystem" is interest. "Sounds cool, let's find synergies" is not.

4. Conversion, not volume. Our history shows the exact failure you're hired to prevent: reps sending 40-60 outreaches a week, reporting "interested projects," and producing no decision-maker conversations and no calls. You own the conversion at every stage:

A. Positive reply ? meaningful advancement within 5 business days. That means a decision-maker conversation, a
 group or direct thread with the right person, or a concrete scheduled next step toward a call. If none occurs, the prospect is recycled or closed out of active pipeline. Claimed interest that never advances counts as nothing.

B. Every live opportunity has one owner, one next action, one deadline.

C. Any opportunity untouched for 5 business days gets a decision: advance, recycle, or close. Nothing sits in "waiting."

D. "Calendly shared" is not a completed task. No booking within 2 business days means follow-up happens, and the prospect is told to confirm the booking with both you and the rep.

E. If significant outreach produces no qualified calls, you identify the failure point (targets, contacts, messaging, channel, follow-up, or rep) and launch a new test within 24 hours. The same broken approach never runs for multiple weeks.



5. Pipeline control. One accurate source of truth: target, category, tier, contact and decision-maker status, owner, every touch, stage, next action, deadline, call status. Duplicate outreach prevented. All partner groups remain accessible to GMI even if a rep leaves.

6. Founder handoff. Before a call goes on the founder's calendar: a short brief covering who they are, why they're qualified, why LP Bonds fit, what interest they expressed, who d
, and the desired outcome. No Calendly shared before the qualification gate is complete.

7. Reporting and escalation. Every Friday YOU post one consolidated report: outreach sent, positive replies, qualified conversations, groups created, calls booked, calls held, conversion at each stage, per-rep results, stalled deals, next week's tests. Exact numbers and names, no narratives. Chasing reps for their numbers is your job, done before Friday, never visible to the founder.

If the week is heading to zero qualified calls, you tell the founder THAT DAY with the likely cause, the numbers, the fix being launched, and when results should show. Bad news early is rewarded. Bad news buried is a dealbreaker.



Time allocation

A. 50%+ on outreach, follow-up, and appointment conversion

B. Up to 25% managing and recruiting reps

C. Up to 25% research, reporting, and admin



Building internal tools, assigning books, refining meeting formats, and polishing trackers do not count toward anything. If the team is below target, your personal outreach time goes up.





First 30 days (paid trial)

Day 3: Full audit of every rep and the current pipeline. Immediate correction plan presented.

Day 7: Clean pipeline and reporting system live. 100+ prioritized qualified targets. Every rep assigned accounts and numbers. Two outreach tests launched. Your personal outreach started.

Day 14: 2+ qualified appointments held. Measurable conversion at each funnel stage. Non-performers cut or on a final clock. Zero held appointments by Day 14 triggers an immediate role review.

Day 30 minimum: 6 qualified appointments held, 2+ in the final week, clean pipeline, producing rep core. Target: 8-10 held, exiting at a 3-5/week pace.



Hit the numbers and this grows into a larger BD leadership role with more hours and higher comp as we scale.



Compensation

A. Base: $10/hr, up to 20 hrs/week

B. $100 for every qualified appointment held that you personally booked

C. $30 override for every qualified appointment held that your reps booked

Partnership revenue, two lanes:

D. Partnerships YOU originated: you earn the full rep-tier package: 25% of upgrade fees for the first 90 days after go-live, then 10% through month 12, plus the bond bonus ladder (+$500 at $10K minted, +$1,000 at $20K, +$5,000 at $100K and every $100K after, cumulative, no ceiling).

E. Partnerships your REPS originated: you earn an override equal to 20% of your rep's commission payouts, paid by GMI on top of their commission, never deducted from them, plus $250 per partnership once $2,500 in cumulative LP Bond value has been minted in that partner's pools (USD value at time of mint, verified on-chain).

Every partnership has exactly one originator of record in our tracker, so lanes never stack on the same deal.

F, Additional bonuses possible for exceptional strategic partnerships

G. No cap on any of the above. One appointment bonus per call ($100 personal OR $30 override, not both)

H. Appointment bonuses paid after the call happens and the founder confirms it met the standard

I. Base and bonuses paid 50/50 in ETH and GMI, exact valuation method provided in writing before you start





Requirements

A. Crypto-native: DEXs, launchpads, liquidity, TVL, ecosystems, no googling required

B. Prior crypto BD, partnerships, lead-gen, or appointment-setting experience with calls you personally booked

C. Experience managing contractors or reps against numbers, and comfortable cutting non-performers

D. Excellent written English, comfortable messaging founders and senior decision-makers

E. Organized: CRMs, trackers,
, X, LinkedIn, email, outreach platforms (we use Saleshandy)

F. 3+ hrs daily overlap with GMT+7/+8

G. Responsive within 10 minutes during your agreed working block unless on a scheduled call





Working standards

Outcomes over activity. Calls held over calls promised. Decision-makers over moderators. Explicit interest over vague networking. Exact numbers over narratives. Problems escalated the day they appear. Every opportunity has an owner, a next action, and a deadline. No hiding bad weeks. No perfecting systems that don't produce calls. The founder never manages your reps.

title: Social Media Content Creator
description:
We’re looking for a creative and highly motivated Social Media Content Creator to join our fast-paced, video-first marketing team. In this role, you'll be responsible for turning long-form videos into a variety of engaging micro-content across platforms like Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and LinkedIn.

If you love creating memes, Reels, quote cards, captions, and interactive content—and enjoy seeing your work drive

real engagement—this is the perfect role for you.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Repurpose long-form video content into short-form posts, including video clips, graphics, memes, and captions

• Create and schedule content across 2–3 assigned platforms (e.g., IG, TikTok, LinkedIn)

• Monitor social media trends and adapt content to stay relevant and on-brand

• Engage with audiences through comments, polls, and interactive replies

• Collaborate with other team members to align content with brand goals and campaigns

• Track content performance and iterate based on insights

• Use AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Midjourney, or similar) to support ideation, captioning, and visual concept – with strong editorial judgement over AI output



DAILY GOALS

• 3–4 Micro Videos (Reels, TikToks, Shorts)

• 2–3 Graphics (Carousels, quote cards, polls)

• 2–3 Written Pieces (Captions, tweets, prompts)

• 1–2 Engagement Posts (Polls, comment replies, shoutouts)



QUALIFICATIONS

• Must be based in the Philippines

• Strong command of English, with the ability to write short, scroll-stopping copy

• Proficient in Canva Pro and comfortable using CapCut, Descript, or similar video editing tools

• Confident using AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Midjourney, or similar) to speed up ideation, drafting, and asset creation - able to write clear prompts and critically edit AI output

• Familiar with content scheduling tools (e.g., Meta Business Suite, Buffer, Adobe Express)

• Understanding of platform differences (IG ? LinkedIn ? TikTok)

• Able to manage time, meet deadlines, and deliver daily content targets



NICE TO HAVE

• Experience with community platforms like Thinkific or Circle

• Familiarity with LinkedIn content formats

• Ability to analyse post performance and apply insights to future content

• Experience prompting AI for video scripting, captions, or visual concepts



If you’re ready to be a part of a dedicated team and are eager to pursue a path of continuous learning and career

title: Twitch VOD Editor for YouTube — Timestamped Segments, A$50 Per Video
description:
I’m Zhad, an Australian Twitch streamer making IRL and Desktop entertainment, challenges and social content. I’m looking for a reliable freelance editor for ongoing, straightforward stream-to-YouTube edits.



I provide the start and end timestamps for each segment. The segment usually starts with my recorded “Hi YouTube” introduction and contains 1–2 hours of footage, occasionally up to 3 hours. You do not need to search entire streams to find a video idea.



Your job:



- Cut dead time, unnecessary repetition, technical interruptions and parts that do not add entertainment or context.

- Keep the video flowing naturally. Preserve the setup and payoff of jokes and conversations.

- Blur the chat area for the first two minutes of the finished video.

- Add my supplied Twitch follow overlay at the beginning, following the supplied reference.

- Export and deliver an upload-ready YouTube video.

- Finished videos will generally be 15–40 minutes, with a maximum of 1 hour. Do not add filler to reach a duration; flag if a shorter edit works better.



This role does not require short-form clips, full-video subtitles, new graphics, music, thumbnails or elaborate effects. Good judgement, understanding conversational English/Australian accents, and reliable delivery matter most.



Pay: A$50 AUD per completed video, including the agreed edit and one minor revision round. Please confirm this rate works for you for the stated scope. Flag whether occasional 3-hour segments fit this rate before accepting work. We agree any exception before editing begins.



We will start with one paid video at the same A$50 rate. If we work well together, I would like an ongoing arrangement. Weekly volume will be agreed; this is freelance, per-video work, not a full-time salary or guaranteed number of projects.



Please include:



- One or two relevant YouTube edits and what you personally edited.

- Confirmation that A$50 AUD per video works for you.

- Your usual turnaround for a timestamped 1–2-hour source segment, and how many videos you can handle weekly.

- Your editing software and ability to download/upload large video files.

- Whether you are comfortable communicating on WhatsApp after we connect.

- One sentence explaining how you decide what to cut while keeping a video entertaining.

- No unpaid test is required. Please send relevant work rather than a large general portfolio.
